# Pinned write preconditions and graph enforcement

All findings below are source analysis at Triplex e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0. No operation or fixture was executed.

## Two preconditions with different comparison points

The public [TransactionPrecondition schema](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Triple.ts#L131-L160) includes TripleLive and EntityState. The [service metadata](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/Triples.ts#L68-L88) exposes both. The operational guide's narrower compare-and-retract explanation does not exhaust this pinned declaration.

TripleLive requires an explicit retract operation with the same ID anywhere in the command. A retract-pattern operation alone does not satisfy the helper. That structural failure produces WriteError before command claim or position allocation. During application, an unsuccessful retract produces TransactionConflictError only when the ID belongs to the TripleLive set. An unconditioned missing retract otherwise contributes zero to the retracted count. Sources: [precondition helpers](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/transactionMetadata.ts#L167-L197), [transaction validation and application](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L259-L318), [conditional retract branch](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L392-L425).

EntityState is checked after nextCommitPosition and before graph projection or application writes. The shared call reads adapter.getByEntity(entityId) with no temporal basis, sorts the returned IDs and a copy of the expected IDs, and compares lengths and elements. The expected array is not deduplicated. SQLite's omitted-basis branch reads all unretracted recorded facts, with no validAt test. Thus order is immaterial, duplicate expected IDs matter, and a currently unretracted future-valid or expired-valid fact participates. There is no entityType or attribute filter in this comparison. Sources: [exact comparison](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L298-L318), [SQLite omitted-basis behavior](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/sqlite/src/SqliteAdapter.ts#L502-L545).

An empty expected array can therefore express that one entity has no unretracted facts in the transaction's current recorded view. It does not express arbitrary predicate, attribute-only or historical/valid-now absence. The precondition requires no matching operation and is checked before the command's own assertions. Concurrent protection additionally depends on the adapter's atomic transaction and serialization contract; this source pass did not establish any new backend result.

Schema declarations and direct service validation must remain separate. The declared union admits only the two tags. The shared transact path does not visibly schema-decode its inputs; its helpers select recognized tags and validate TripleLive's matching retract. This is a source-level admission boundary for a future adapter or host wrapper, not a claim that every public entrypoint accepts malformed input or that a malformed call failed at runtime.

## Command ordering and serialization

The shared service opens adapter.withTransaction around validation, ID/time acquisition, command claim, position allocation, preconditions, graph enforcement, ordered application and metadata persistence. It batches consecutive assertions but flushes them before a following retract or retract-pattern. Pattern reads therefore occur at their position in the command, after prior assertion batches. This ordering must not be replaced with an unconditional retractions-first API. Sources: [transaction implementation](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L248-L471), [StorageAdapter contract](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/storage/StorageAdapter.ts#L16-L40).

The documented adapter obligation is rollback of facts, retractions, command claims, journal and position allocation together on typed failure, defect or interruption inside that transaction boundary. SQLite's transactional position upsert is inside its SQL transaction; that is a reference implementation shape, not a new runtime proof. The [operational contract](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/docs/operational-primitives.md) explicitly retains global serialization for graph absence and uniqueness protection. A global position used only as an external sequence would not by itself establish that protection. Alternative scoped concurrency remains deferred at this pin.

The standalone retract helper adds a result check after transact returns: when the returned count is not exactly one, it reports WriteError. A missing unconditioned transact retraction can therefore commit a no-op command's position and empty-change envelope before the helper reports an error. A helper error alone is not proof that no position or envelope committed. This is a source deduction, not an observed lost acknowledgement or executed defect. Source: [standalone helper](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L473-L487).

Error ordering also matters. EntityState is checked once before graph enforcement. Graph enforcement precedes application-time TripleLive checks, so a graph violation can be reported before a stale conditional retract. A preceding pattern retraction or a second explicit retract can cause a later guarded retract to return false even when that fact was live at transaction entry. Matching-retract validation does not require exactly one occurrence. No such sequence was executed here.

## Relevant graph and typed identities

The opt-in rule families are Required, Cardinality, Unique and ReferenceTarget, each version 1. Current live-recorded source type rows identify existing subjects; complete facts for those subjects and target type rows are added. Assertions introducing a source type also expand the subject set before projection. The final projected command still decides which subjects are visible at each instant. Source: [rules and bounded loading](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L8-L148).

For each validAt, subject membership means a visible fact carries the rule's entityType field. All visible facts on those entity IDs can satisfy the constrained attribute, including rows without that field themselves. The entityType field is not interchangeable with an application EAV assertion whose attribute happens to mean type.

Required and Cardinality count matching fact rows, including separate assertions with equal values. Unique instead builds a set of entity claimants per canonical tagged storage value. Repeated equal rows on one entity do not create multiple uniqueness claimants. The value key preserves storage tags; blobs include MIME type, size and optional filename as well as content identity. Reusing flattened Datalog scalar equality here would merge identities that this gate distinguishes. Sources: [value identity](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L150-L163), [subject selection and row counts](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L175-L249).

ReferenceTarget requires a ref-tagged source value and some simultaneously visible target fact on that entity carrying targetEntityType. Equal plain string text is insufficient. Required target existence can vary with valid time, so checking only the command instant is insufficient. Source: [reference branch](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L254-L280).

## New or worsened findings at every represented valid boundary

Projection applies operations sequentially, uses command time for omitted validFrom, and removes pattern matches from the current projected collection. Only the final projected state is evaluated, not every intermediate operation state. The enforcement gate enumerates the sorted distinct validFrom and present validTo boundaries of both current and projected relevant facts, including boundaries of removed facts. It compares before and after independently at each boundary using half-open validity. This is enforcement over the current recorded view, not revalidation of every historical recorded-time cut. Sources: [sequential projection](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L303-L361), [boundary gate](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/Constraint.ts#L364-L397).

A finding is rejected when its identity was absent before or its actual count increases. Identity includes constraint key, code, subject, attribute and optional value identity. An unchanged pre-existing violation is allowed; a lower cardinality/claimant count can repair it without reaching a clean graph. Moving a violation to a new subject or value creates a new identity even if a global total is unchanged. A clean-state validator would reject more commands than this contract, while a check only at now would miss future or historical valid-time violations.

Subject existence itself is temporal. Removing every visible typed fact from an entity can remove it from a rule's subject set rather than creating a Required finding for a persistent external entity registry. This follows the inspected fact-based subject selection; it is not a claim that the system enforces entity lifecycle policy or authorization.

Enforcement is opt-in per command through supplied rules. The inspected service does not verify that those rules correspond to configSnapshot or require that metadata field. It does not establish authorization, a persistent database constraint or protection against direct adapter writes. The exact plain rule schemas use Schema.Number for cardinality max, while public GraphConstraint constructors/config parsing separately validate a positive safe integer. The inspected transact path does not prove complete runtime rule admission or canonical-encoding success. Sources: [enforcement entry](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/store/TriplesLive.ts#L320-L361), [constructor and parsing checks](https://github.com/bjacobso/triplex/blob/e24dcdbfce4e61da3e2f08c0e4f2a4531c7df0a0/packages/core/src/config/GraphConstraint.ts#L94-L157).

The pure evaluateFacts helper itself filters validity only. Its current-recorded input premise comes from the loader/caller, rather than a retractedAt check inside the evaluator. This research selects no malformed-rule policy and claims no executed defect. A future adapter selection needs explicit validated rule/input and recorded-view boundaries rather than inferring them from TypeScript types.
